system.title: What is a System of Equations?
system.intro: A system of equations is a set of two or more equations with the same variables that we solve together.
system.explanation: We need to find values of x and y that make BOTH equations true at the same time!

notes.title: Tips and Tricks

solution.content: The solution to a system is an ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies ALL equations in the system. Think of it as finding the point where two paths cross!

notes.tip1: Choose the method that looks easiest! If one equation is already solved for a variable, use substitution.
notes.tip2: If coefficients of a variable are the same or opposites, use elimination.
notes.tip3: Always check your solution by substituting back into BOTH original equations!

tickets.title: 🎫 Concert Tickets
tickets.problem: You bought 50 tickets (adult and child) for $650. Adult tickets cost $15 and child tickets cost $10. How many of each did you buy?
tickets.note: This system helps us find how many adult (a) and child (c) tickets were purchased!

graphing.title: Method 1: Graphing
graphing.description: Graph both equations on the same coordinate plane. The solution is where the lines intersect (cross)!

substitution.title: Method 2: Substitution
substitution.description: Solve one equation for a variable, then substitute that expression into the other equation.

elimination.title: Method 3: Elimination (Addition/Subtraction)
elimination.description: Add or subtract the equations to eliminate one variable, then solve for the remaining variable.

graphing.title: Key Point About Graphing:
graphing.content: The intersection point represents values that satisfy BOTH equations simultaneously. If lines don't intersect, there's no solution!

one.title: One Solution
one.description: Lines intersect at exactly one point. The system is CONSISTENT and INDEPENDENT.

none.title: No Solution
none.description: Lines are parallel (never intersect). The system is INCONSISTENT.

infinite.title: Infinitely Many Solutions
infinite.description: Lines are the same (coincide). The system is CONSISTENT and DEPENDENT.

exercise1.question: Solve the system: x + y = 5 and x - y = -1. What is the solution?
exercise1.explanation: Adding the equations: 2x = 4, so x = 2. Substitute: 2 + y = 5, so y = 3. Solution: (2, 3)

exercise2.question: Using substitution, solve: y = 2x and x + y = 12. What is the value of x?
exercise2.hint: Substitute y = 2x into the second equation.

exercise3.question: Two lines have equations y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x - 3. How many solutions does this system have?
exercise3.explanation: The lines have the same slope (2) but different y-intercepts, so they are parallel and never intersect. No solution.

exercise4.question: Solve using elimination: 2x + y = 14 and 2x - y = 6. What is the value of y? Enter the number.
exercise4.hint: Subtract the second equation from the first to eliminate x.
exercise4.explanation: Subtracting: (2x + y) - (2x - y) = 14 - 6 gives 2y = 8, so y = 4. Then find x: 2x + 4 = 14, x = 5. But we only need y = 4.

exercise5.question: A system of equations has the solution (3, 5). Which equation must be in the system?
exercise5.explanation: Check (3, 5) in each: 3 + 5 = 8 ✓. The answer is x + y = 8.

exercise6.question: Solve: 2x + y = 12 and x = 2. What is the value of y? Enter the number.
exercise6.hint: Substitute x = 2 into the first equation.

conclusion.title: Mastering Systems of Equations!
conclusion.summary: You've learned three powerful methods to solve systems of equations. Each method has its advantages depending on the problem!
conclusion.takeaway1: A system solution must satisfy ALL equations
conclusion.takeaway2: Graphing shows the visual relationship between equations
conclusion.takeaway3: Substitution works well when a variable is already isolated
conclusion.takeaway4: Elimination is efficient when coefficients line up nicely
